figures.caption: Fig. 9.5.4, the primary side of the combiner has two pairs of differential ports excited by outphasing signals while the center taps provide DC access. The unwanted magnetic coupling of adjacent windings is minimized by orthogonal placement of the two coils. This combiner has a -1dB BW of 20GHz which guarantees correct outphasing operation.

references.sentence: As shown in the system diagram of Fig. 9.5.1, the outphasing TX requires constant-amplitude phase-modulated baseband signals SI1(t), SI2(t) and SQ1(t), SQ2(t) where θ(t) indicates the modulated phase and the outphasing angle ϕ(t) determines the instantaneous amplitude (ϕ(t) = cos-1[a(t)/2A]).
Figure 9.5.2 shows the implementation of the I/Q double-balanced mixer, which is tuned at 60GHz by a transformer and 35μm interconnects.
The PA incorporates two unit PAs with a power combiner at the output (see Fig. 9.5.1).
As shown in Fig. 9.5.4, the primary side of the combiner has two pairs of differential ports excited by outphasing signals while the center taps provide DC access.
Mismatch between the two outphasing signals S1(t) and S2(t) (see Fig. 9.5.1) is a potential cause of amplitude and phase distortion.
Figure 9.5.7 shows the die micrograph and the TX measures 0.96mm2.
Figure 9.5.3 shows that the TX has a measured conversion gain of 26dB and the –3dB RF BW is more than 7GHz (59.5 to 67 GHz).

The two major benefits of the TX in outphasing mode are demonstrated in Fig. 9.5.4, which shows the measured output power and the PA power consumption for both outphasing and conventional direct-conversion modes.
Figure 9.5.5 shows that the outphasing mode achieves >13dBm PAVG and >15% average PA efficiency (ηAVG = PAVG/PDC,PA) for both QPSK and 8PSK at the EVM of -25dB.
Figure 9.5.6 compares the measured performance with other 60GHz transmitters, clearly showing the improved efficiency and higher linear output power of the presented outphasing TX.
